exposure: cervical os dilatation at the diagnosis of the active phase of labour
cohort: Low-risk singleton pregnancies at or beyond 37 weeks with spontaneous onset of labor
finding: A cervical dilation of 6 cm at the diagnosis of active labor was associated with a reduced risk of caesarean section and an increased need for analgesia, without significant differences in other maternal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: A cervical os dilatation of 6 cm reduces the risk of caesarean section by 11%.
